Core to number theory (500/869 = 57% hard) — constraint propagation through congruence classes. The high Level 5 count confirms that deep modular chains define the hardest subclass.

reasoning_style_comparison.algebra: Algebra is the largest domain (1744 problems) with 834/1744 = 47% hard problems. Its balanced level distribution indicates that algebraic reasoning spans a wide difficulty range from direct formula application to multi-step symbolic transformation.
reasoning_style_comparison.geometry: Geometry has the highest hard-problem concentration: 598/870 = 68% hard, with Level 5 = 421 problems (48%). This extreme Level 5 skew confirms that multi-step auxiliary construction problems dominate the hardest subclass.
reasoning_style_comparison.counting_and_probability: Counting and probability (771 problems, 442/771 = 57% hard). Level 5 problems require recognizing the correct recursive state decomposition.
reasoning_style_comparison.number_theory: Number theory (869 problems, 500/869 = 57% hard). Level 5 = 313 problems (36%). Modular arithmetic and divisibility analysis define the reasoning style; Level 5 requires multi-modulus non-constructive arguments.
reasoning_style_comparison.precalculus: Precalculus (746 problems, 352/746 = 47% hard) has the most balanced level distribution. Level 5 problems require the deepest analytic function composition chains.

cross_domain_reasoning_transfer: Ranked by hard-problem rate: geometry (68%) > number_theory (57%) > counting (57%) > algebra (47%) > precalculus (47%). Geometry's dominance (Level 5 = 421/870 = 48%) reflects that spatial reasoning combined with multi-step construction is structurally harder than any other proof pattern.
